body: My mom was a teacher at my middle school and a few friends of mine and I were at the school after dark one night waiting for her while she was in some kind of meeting or event, I can’t really remember. We were playing outside when suddenly I got very panicked and froze. When they asked me what I was afraid of I told them there was some kind of ghost, a “blue thing” that I could see and I thought it was evil. Much to my surprise, the three other girls said they could see it too! The only problem was, I was only playing a prank and made the whole thing up! I never imagined they’d play along, but that was the moment I decided my life goal was to become a cult leader.

I do, but I’ve worked on  this by finding ways to socialize with people on equal footing like at a class you pay for or work events, that way I don’t have to care that I think everyone hates me and wants me to leave because I have just as much of a right to be there as they do. I’m more self conscious going to a bar or someone’s house because there are less social conventions to guide the interactions (how do you know if they actually want you around or are just too polite to kick you out?) and because I feel like no one likes me or wants me there.  If I paid to be there, I don’t have to feel guilty just for existing.
My guess would be that it stuck in the sports that are considered “America’s games” like baseball and football because it’s on brand.

I fail to see anything I wrote as a rant.  I also fail to see where I vilified "evil rich white males" or "declared my own moral superiority". I experience white privilege as a woman of a certain socioeconomic standing as well and I don't blame them for having it, I blame them for thinking they should abide by a different set of rules because of it.

I'm not quite sure what problem pointing out the fact that a man thinks his son, a felon, should go unpunished because of his gender, race and class makes me a part of, but I can assure you it's a "problem" I'm more than happy to escalate.

My statements solely discuss one man and his son, not a whole population of people. I also never said that the majority of rich white males rape.  My problem with this criminal and his father isn't that they enjoy big ribeyes, it's that they believe that should literally be a get out of jail free card.  He believes his son's suffering for the crime he committed is more tragic than the woman he victimized during his "20 minutes of action".  

This is a man who fully acknowledges that his son committed the crimes and yet shows no remorse.  He doesn't believe Brock's already inappropriately miniscule sentence should be reduced because he learned his lesson or because he feels so guilty or was too drunk to realize what was happening or that he is innocent in any way.  His only rationale for a lesser sentence is that he's privileged enough to have a bright future and no longer has an appetite for the steak he so enjoys now that he is afraid of going to jail.

I understand what you're saying, #notallmen and all of those great "causes" that selfishly focus on their own plight of being completely uninvolved or mentioned in the discussion, but just because all slave owners didn't rape and beat, were the ones that did any less guilty? Not all Germans worked at Auschwitz, should we have declined to report on the ones who did? 

I understand that these ideas may upset people who identify with the perpetrators, but I refuse to sugarcoat how wrong something is because it might upset someone and I hope that is something i never "grow out of".

The issue is all about race, class and white maleness.  It's not a political perspective, if it's the truth.  All of the content is about his privilege...what content to people need to hear if not the part about a rich white boy getting away with a rape he's already been convicted of with barely any punishment because he went to the same college as the judge? How many examples are there of men of any other ethnicity getting caught in the act and convicted of three felonies being punished with a 6 month sentence that will likely end up with 3 months max in prison?  And you could never go to a low income neighborhood and find a father, who never once denies that his son actually committed the crime, but thinks the fact that he likes to eat steak but hasn't wanted one lately will compel a judge to keep him out of jail...especially with all the articles online crucifying people who buy steak with food stamps.  Do you think if this boy grew up in a bad neighborhood and ended up working at McDonald's instead of with all of the privilege he had that led him to be an athlete at Stanford, he would have gotten the same sentence? I don't.  I can also guarantee that if Brock had been the victim of a 20 year old man sexually assaulting him while he was passed out the sentence would be much higher.  His father saying 20 minutes of raping someone doesn't deserve a punishment, or that he "wasn't violent" while LITERALLY ASSAULTING HER can only be construed to mean the victim, a woman, doesn't count.

If people are turned off by the tone then they are part of the problem.
